chosen.premise: Mr. Mime’s pantomime can turn an invisible object into something real once observers believe in it.
chosen.hook: What if pretending hard enough made imaginary things real?
chosen.visualIdea: Show Mr. Mime miming an invisible object, then make it appear the instant a crowd reacts.
chosen.note: An unusually specific Mr. Mime premise, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries; the belief-triggered transformation creates a strong visual payoff.

candidates.premise: Mr. Mime’s invisible walls come from fingertip vibrations that stop air molecules in midair.
candidates.hook: Mr. Mime doesn’t just mime a wall—it stops the air itself.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom from vibrating fingertips to air molecules locking into a transparent wall against an attack.
candidates.note: Concrete and highly visual, with direct Pokédex support, though the scientific explanation risks sounding like an extrapolation from fictional lore.

candidates.premise: Interrupt Mr. Mime’s act and its invisible performance ends with a broad-handed slap—or a DoubleSlap.
candidates.hook: The fastest way to get attacked by Mr. Mime is to interrupt the show.
candidates.visualIdea: Cut off a silent pantomime mid-gesture, then snap to Mr. Mime’s hands delivering a cartoonish slap.
candidates.note: Very well supported and easy to stage, but the joke is more of a familiar character trait than a deeply surprising discovery.

candidates.premise: Galar’s Mr. Mime is taller and heavier than the original, and its typing changes from Psychic/Fairy to Ice/Psychic.
candidates.hook: Galar changes Mr. Mime’s type—and adds height and weight.
candidates.visualIdea: Place both forms side by side with type icons, height markers, and weights changing from 1.3m/54.5kg to 1.4m/56.8kg.
candidates.note: Excellent data and comparison graphics, but regional-form stat and typing changes are a common Pokémon angle and less emotionally intriguing.

candidates.premise: Mime Jr. becomes Mr. Mime by leveling up while knowing Mimic—the move is part of the evolution requirement.
candidates.hook: Mr. Mime’s evolution requires it to know one move: Mimic.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Mime Jr. copying a move, then trigger the evolution into Mr. Mime with the Mimic requirement highlighted.
candidates.note: A precise evolution rule with good fan appeal; its support relies on the trusted-secondary evolution data, and the visual payoff is comparatively conventional.

candidates.premise: Mr. Mime’s unusually broad hands may have enlarged specifically to improve its pantomime.
candidates.hook: Those huge hands may exist because Mr. Mime is a professional mime.
candidates.visualIdea: Outline Mr. Mime’s broad palms, then connect their size to gestures, invisible walls, and slaps.
candidates.note: The hand-size explanation is distinctive and visual, but the source presents it as a scientific belief rather than an established fact, and the surprise is modest.

rounds.request: Not applicable: belief-makes-real is strong enough to lead the episode. Stronger alternatives would need an equally specific, canon-backed mechanism with a surprising visual transformation.
